title: PHAGE-BLOOD – Phage efficacy and immune response in critical infections: a prospective in-vitro and ex-vivo observational study
summary: This study evaluates whether bacteriophages, viruses that specifically kill bacteria, are effective against pathogens causing severe infections such as sepsis or endocarditis. Laboratory experiments are performed on patient samples to measure bacterial killing and immune responses. The study is observational and involves only an additional blood draw, without therapeutic intervention.

interventions.name:
Adult patients with suspected
sepsis (Sepsis-3 criteria) or
infective endocarditis (modified Duke criteria),
undergoing routine blood culture diagnostics. Additional EDTA blood samples are collected for immunological testing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspected sepsis with blood cultures and SOFA increase ≥ 2
or suspected infective endocarditis
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal or withdrawal of consent
